ME.take: In the Gulf, the war rewarded asset-light rerouting capacity and punished fixed hubs: Aramex and Agility grew revenue by 22-26% selling alternative routes, charters and ground handling, while DP World grew revenue 13% but lost 60% of Jebel Ali volume and saw adjusted EBITDA fall. For cross-border e-commerce into the GCC, our read is that landed cost and transit time stay structurally higher while cargo moves via Khor Fakkan, Fujairah and overland corridors, and that capacity on those routes, not hub scale, is the scarce asset until Hormuz traffic normalises.

companies.name: Aramex

Net margin still thin at 2.6%

dnata revenue +12% to AED23.6bn, 77% earned outside the UAE

SkyCargo revenue broadly flat despite added capacity

companies.exposure: The Middle East conflict disrupted Dubai hub operations from late February, on top of weaker cargo yields.

companies.name: DP World
companies.vs_prev: Hormuz impact deepened through the half: Jebel Ali handled 374,000 TEU in Q2 (-90.1% YoY) after a less affected Q1; profit attributable to owners fell 47.3% to US$280m.
companies.volume: Gross throughput 42.8m TEU (-5.7%); excluding Jebel Ali 39.7m TEU (+6.5% like-for-like); Jebel Ali 3.1m TEU (-59.5%)
highlights: Logistics, Parks and Economic Zones revenue +24.2% to US$5.9bn
International ports outside Jebel Ali growing, Australia and Americas EBITDA +25.9%
Two new Fujairah terminals planned under a 50-year concession to reduce Hormuz dependence
challenges: Strait of Hormuz disruption cut vessel calls at Jebel Ali; infrastructure undamaged but idle capacity kept on standby
Leverage up to 3.7x net debt/adjusted EBITDA (3.4x at end-2025)
Capex of about US$3.0bn planned for 2026 while core hub earnings are depressed
companies.outlook: Near-term environment uncertain; management positive on medium to long-term global trade; 2026 capex guided at about US$3.0bn.
companies.exposure: Hormuz disruption cut vessel calls at Jebel Ali, and the Fujairah terminals are its answer to reduce dependence on the strait.

companies.vs_prev: SPL is state-owned and does not publish periodic financial results; Naqel Express, fully acquired by SPL, is not separately reported.

NAF.take: Morocco's gateways keep compounding: Tanger Med closed 2025 with revenue +16% and operating profit +23%, and Marsa Maroc grew H1 2026 EBITDA 20% on 3% more tonnage, so pricing and logistics services are driving earnings rather than volume alone. Our read is that growth is increasingly led by domestic trade (Marsa Maroc transshipment -4%), while the e-commerce last mile remains thin and loss-making: Jumia grows orders 26% but still burns cash, and the national post discloses no parcel economics.
